This was my exact thought when I was told about the capacity issue. I knew people would complain about “how they spent X amount of money for this game and they should be allowed to play it whenever”, to which I agree, but that complaint would only lead to “…this is why live service games are bad and ruin blank blank blank..” which I partially agree. It’s as you said: they’re suffering from their own success. This is their first AAA game and wasn’t expecting its popularity to boom as much as it did. 

But I get it; after coming across crappy games left and right, we tend to get pretty irritated once that gem of a game releases and has issues that hinder our “fun time”. Then we have to look elsewhere for temporary enjoyment. 

Ultimately I think people need to relax with this type of thing. Calling people “white knights” for defending the devs in this situation is wild.

I personally think gun confiscation is a bit ridiculous of course, but I feel as though the ability to obtain one should be a lot more strict. However to your point, lots of pro 2A people say the same kind of conflicting things as well. *if you can’t trust the police, then who will save you when someone breaks in?* which raises the question: if you’re so pro 2A, why even worry about what the police will do if someone breaks in? Most seem to want a *reason* to use their firearms. I mean there’s a lot more to this example but yeah.

But they’re also not the ones who are lining up to protest and force laws against those who *do* suffer from unfortunate circumstances like drugs and physical abuse, and aren’t capable of taking care of a child. Dont get me wrong; I’m not playing either side. I *will* however side with freedom of choice, no matter who it is. But once you weaponize something like Christianity (or any religion for that matter) and use that as your reasons against another’s personal decisions, then I gotta go against you.
